To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DNA thermodynamics shape chromosome architecture and topology.
the DNA sequence encodes the thermodynamics, supercoiling and topology of DNA, which in turn specify the organization of the genome and the structure of chromatin.
DNA thermodynamics and topology are interdependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physical and topological properties that govern the structure of the genome and the chromatin fiber.
the interplay between DNA thermodynamics and the topological and mechanical properties of chromosomes, and the consequences for genome organization and function.
the physical principles of the organization of DNA into chromatin and its biological significance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the DNA sequence of the genome contains the instructions for the construction of the chromosome, and that these instructions are not encoded by the sequence itself, but rather by the thermodynamic properties of the DNA sequence.

the DNA sequence is a primary determinant of chromosome organization and that the DNA sequence, DNA topology and DNA thermodynamics act in concert to specify the structure of chromosomes and chromatin.
DNA thermodynamics shape chromosome topology and organization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DNA sequence of the genome is the primary source of the chromatin organization.

DNA sequences encode information that can be used to organize the genome in a hierarchical fashion, with DNA sequences encoding the information that can be exploited by DNA topoisomerases to generate superhelical tension and by DNA translocases to move DNA in a direction that can lead to the formation of topologically distinct chromatin structures.
DNA thermodynamics shape chromosome topology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DNA sequence of a genome is an important source of topological information that is encoded by DNA thermodynamics and is transmitted to the chromosome by the action of translocases.
the DNA sequence of the genome contains a wealth of information about its own organization.
the DNA sequence encodes not only the genetic information, but also the mechanical and topological characteristics of the genome.
